headline: I run construction projects, and I build
intro: Ten years managing regulated, mission-critical projects in the Bay Area, from schools to a hospital campus to historic renovation. Along the way I started writing the tools I kept wishing I had.

problem.title: Where projects quietly lose time and money
problem.body: On a real job the work lives in RFIs, submittals, change orders, cost reports and email threads, scattered across Procore and everyone's inbox. Most of it is manual, and it is where schedule and budget slip without anyone noticing. Years in the field, in the office and in the owner meeting showed me exactly where it breaks.

approach.title: Tools that sit on top of how projects really run
approach.body: I don't try to replace Procore or the way a team works. I connect what is already there, pull it into one view, and let AI do the first draft, while a person who knows the job reviews it before anything goes out.
